title: Comparison of projection-inverse tensor composites before adjunction
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $i:Z\to T$ be a proper morphism of schemes with $T$ quasi-compact [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module derived categories $D(W_e,A)$ and $D(W_p,A)$ on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Write $C_W=\nu_W^*$ for the termwise exact comparison pullback [def-sf-comparison-derived-pullback], $F_e=Ri_{e,*}$ and $F_p=Ri_{p,*}$. Use the canonical tensor comparison $c_{W;U,V}:C_W(U\otimes_A^LV)\xrightarrow{\sim}C_WU\otimes_A^LC_WV$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], the ordinary pullback comparison $\rho_M:i_p^*C_TM\xrightarrow{\sim}C_Zi_e^*M$ [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and the signed tensor symmetry $\sigma$ (on homogeneous degrees $a,b$, the swap multiplied by $(-1)^{ab}$). Let $\eta:F_pC_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}C_TF_e$ be a natural comparison isomorphism. On each site use the ordinary-counit-defined projection transformation $\pi^\tau_{B,M}:F_\tau B\otimes_A^LM\to F_\tau(B\otimes_A^Li_\tau^*M)$, defined by the same composite as [def-kun-projection-formula-map].

Let $B\in D^+(Z_e,A)$, $M,Y\in D^+(T_e,A)$, $B'\in D^+(Z_p,A)$, $v:C_ZB\xrightarrow{\sim}B'$, and arrows $a_e:F_eB\to Y$ and $a_p:F_pB'\to C_TY$. Suppose
$$a_p\circ F_p(v)=C_T(a_e)\circ\eta_B.$$
Define
$$s=(\rho_M^{-1}\otimes v)\circ c_{Z;i_e^*M,B}:C_Z(i_e^*M\otimes_A^LB)\xrightarrow{\sim}i_p^*C_TM\otimes_A^LB',$$
$$r=(v\otimes\rho_M^{-1})\circ c_{Z;B,i_e^*M}:C_Z(B\otimes_A^Li_e^*M)\xrightarrow{\sim}B'\otimes_A^Li_p^*C_TM.$$
Assume $\pi_e=\pi^e_{B,M}$ and $\pi_p=\pi^p_{B',C_TM}$ are isomorphisms and that their comparison square is
$$\eta_{B\otimes_A^Li_e^*M}\circ F_p(r^{-1})\circ\pi_p\circ(F_p(v)\otimes1)=C_T(\pi_e)\circ c_{T;F_eB,M}^{-1}\circ(\eta_B\otimes1).$$
Define the two untransposed composites
$$t_e=(1_M\otimes a_e)\circ\sigma_{F_eB,M}\circ\pi_e^{-1}\circ F_e(\sigma_{i_e^*M,B}):F_e(i_e^*M\otimes_A^LB)\to M\otimes_A^LY,$$
$$t_p=(1_{C_TM}\otimes a_p)\circ\sigma_{F_pB',C_TM}\circ\pi_p^{-1}\circ F_p(\sigma_{i_p^*C_TM,B'}):F_p(i_p^*C_TM\otimes_A^LB')\to C_TM\otimes_A^LC_TY.$$
Then
$$c_{T;M,Y}\circ C_T(t_e)\circ\eta_{i_e^*M\otimes_A^LB}=t_p\circ F_p(s).$$
No exceptional right adjoint, constructibility of $B$, or finite Tor amplitude of $B$ is required; only the displayed projection components are assumed invertible.

proof.text:
Work in the ambient unbounded derived categories, abbreviating $\otimes_A^L$ to $\otimes$, $C_T$ to $C$, and $i_e^*M$ to $L$. The comparison morphism $\nu_W$ is a morphism of ringed topoi with its constant-$A$ structural map; its module pullback is exact, so its total left derived pullback is the termwise functor $C_W$ specified in the statement. Apply the canonical ringed-topos tensor comparison to $\nu_W$. Its naturality and its compatibility with the signed symmetry give, for arrows $f:U\to U'$ and $g:V\to V'$,
$$c_{W;U',V'}C_W(f\otimes g)=(C_Wf\otimes C_Wg)c_{W;U,V},\qquad c_{W;V,U}C_W(\sigma_{U,V})=\sigma_{C_WU,C_WV}c_{W;U,V}.$$
The signed symmetries on both sites are natural in both variables. These are statements of the three cited nodes, applied to the small site representatives in a universe containing the module sheaves. No special property of $i$, $B$ or $M$ is needed for them. All subsequent tensor products and comparisons are in these ambient categories; bounded-below inputs need not have bounded-below derived tensor products.

proof.text:
Put $D=L\otimes B$, $E=B\otimes L$, $L'=i_p^*CM$, and write $\sigma_e=\sigma_{L,B}$ and $\sigma_p=\sigma_{L',B'}$. The definitions of $r,s$ and the symmetry equation of step 1, followed by naturality of the pro-etale symmetry for $\rho_M^{-1}:C_ZL\to L'$ and $v:C_ZB\to B'$, give
$$r\,C_Z(\sigma_e)=(v\otimes\rho_M^{-1})\sigma_{C_ZL,C_ZB}c_{Z;L,B}=\sigma_p(\rho_M^{-1}\otimes v)c_{Z;L,B}=\sigma_p s.$$
Set $H=\eta_E F_p(r^{-1})$. Applying $F_p$, cancelling $F_p(r^{-1})F_p(r)$, and using naturality of the given $\eta$ at $\sigma_e:D\to E$, yields the input identity
$$H F_p(\sigma_p)F_p(s)=\eta_E F_p(C_Z\sigma_e)=C(F_e\sigma_e)\eta_D.$$
Thus the two different tensor orders in $r$ and $s$ have been accounted for explicitly.

proof.text:
Define the isomorphisms $V=F_p(v)$, $d=\eta_B V^{-1}:F_pB'\to C(F_eB)$, and $k=c_{T;F_eB,M}$. The assumed projection square is exactly
$$H\pi_p(V\otimes1)=C(\pi_e)k^{-1}(\eta_B\otimes1).$$
Compose on the left with $k\,C(\pi_e^{-1})$ and on the right with $(V^{-1}\otimes1)\pi_p^{-1}$. Functoriality and the inverse laws cancel $C(\pi_e^{-1})C(\pi_e)$, $k k^{-1}$, $V^{-1}V$, and $\pi_p\pi_p^{-1}$. The result is
$$k C(\pi_e^{-1})H=(d\otimes1)\pi_p^{-1}.$$
This inverts only the two projection components stipulated to be invertible; it does not invoke any projection-formula theorem.

proof.text:
Put $g_e=(1_M\otimes a_e)\sigma_{F_eB,M}$ and $g_p=(1_{CM}\otimes a_p)\sigma_{F_pB',CM}$. The hypothesis on the final arrows, after composition with $V^{-1}$, says $a_p=C(a_e)d$. Naturality of the tensor comparison for $(1_M,a_e)$ and its symmetry equation give
$$c_{T;M,Y}C(g_e)=(1_{CM}\otimes C(a_e))\sigma_{C(F_eB),CM}\,k.$$
Naturality of the signed pro-etale symmetry at $d:F_pB'\to C(F_eB)$ gives
$$(1_{CM}\otimes C(a_e))\sigma_{C(F_eB),CM}(d\otimes1)=(1_{CM}\otimes C(a_e)d)\sigma_{F_pB',CM}=g_p.$$
Since $d$ is invertible, these two equations yield the output identity
$$c_{T;M,Y}C(g_e)=g_p(d^{-1}\otimes1)k.$$
This uses the given arrow compatibility, rather than assuming that an arbitrary final arrow is preserved by comparison.

proof.text:
By definition $t_e=g_e\pi_e^{-1}F_e(\sigma_e)$ and $t_p=g_p\pi_p^{-1}F_p(\sigma_p)$. Substitute the input identity from step 2, the output identity from step 4, and the inverse-projection identity from step 3 in that order:
$$\begin{aligned}
c_{T;M,Y}C(t_e)\eta_D
&=c_{T;M,Y}C(g_e)C(\pi_e^{-1})H F_p(\sigma_p)F_p(s)\\
&=g_p(d^{-1}\otimes1)k C(\pi_e^{-1})H F_p(\sigma_p)F_p(s)\\
&=g_p(d^{-1}\otimes1)(d\otimes1)\pi_p^{-1}F_p(\sigma_p)F_p(s)\\
&=t_pF_p(s).
\end{aligned}$$
The last cancellation is tensor bifunctoriality and $d^{-1}d=1$. Since $D=i_e^*M\otimes_A^LB$, this is the asserted equality. The argument never forms an exceptional right adjoint or uses constructibility or finite Tor amplitude of $B$.

tool_uses.why: Canonical derived pullback tensor comparison is natural on arbitrary ringed sites; this generic fact is needed at nu_T and nu_Z and is not supplied by the boundary-biduality unit.
